logo_process.shared_prompt: Premium conceptual identity symbol for The Human Touch, a museum-led human–machine co-presence brand. Produce one standalone image: exactly one simple abstract mark, full square canvas, cropped with roughly 15% clear margin. Flat solid deep burgundy ink #551F30 on genuinely transparent background. Extremely refined bold optical geometry, editorial museum quality, readable at 32px, intentional negative space. No words, letters, faces, profiles, heads, brains, humans, robots, fingers, hands, hearts, generic infinity symbols, circuitry, gear wheels, gradients, shading, photos or mockups. The concept:

variants.name: Tangent
variants.prompt: Two unequal solid wedges approach on the diagonal: a broad round convex end meets a small flat plane at precisely one point. Build a compact offset square silhouette and make the contact point readable.

variants.name: Fulcrum
variants.prompt: A low, weighty asymmetric horizontal beam is balanced on one tapered upright at its off-center equilibrium point. Sculptural cantilever, conveying a partner taking the other end of a load. Thick and stable.

variants.name: Dovetail
variants.prompt: A simple chunky interlocking dovetail joint: an organic wedge with a softened shoulder locks into a geometrically cut rectangular mate. One clean diagonal sliver of negative space distinguishes the two fitted parts.

variants.name: Interleaf
variants.prompt: Two solid folded leaves of paper slip through one another at a right angle; a single crisp over-under break reveals mutual support. A compact three-quarter folded corner shape, not a loop or chain.

variants.name: Interval
variants.prompt: Two hefty offset upright slabs stand apart; their inner edges define one precise vibrating hourglass-shaped pocket of air. The void rather than the outer form is the visual subject. Minimal sharp/soft tension.

variants.name: Counterform
variants.prompt: An asymmetric solid disk is split by one stepped joint: an angular indentation on one side and a single gently cupped protrusion on the other fit one another perfectly. The dividing slit remains visible. Avoid yin-yang.

variants.name: Weft
variants.prompt: Three substantial square-ended horizontal warp bars and ONE supple diagonal ribbon pass over and under one another, reduced to a compact memorable woven stamp, distinct rhythm, legible negative channels.

variants.name: Cadence
variants.prompt: A low horizontal sequence of three bold abstract pressure impressions. One is compressed and the next gently expands, anchored along a common baseline; evokes the cadence of a cue and a response. Not sound wave bars.

variants.name: Shared Span
variants.prompt: Two distinct corbels reach inward from opposite low bases at slightly different levels, supporting one continuous long lintel. Open asymmetric architectural span, side elevation, no conventional arch.

variants.name: Meniscus
variants.prompt: Two horizontal solids briefly touch and form a small smooth meniscus bridge between them, like capillary contact. Show one minimal, sculptural solid outline with two generous open lateral concavities at the contact. No droplets or circles.

board_process.prompt: Create a complete museum brand identity system in one beautifully art-directed 3:2 landscape image for 'The Human Touch'. The first reference is the exact newly chosen logo: a compact squared DOVETAIL sign made of a curved burgundy piece and chamfered piece joined along a diagonal slit. Match this symbol EXACTLY every time. The symbol must stay completely abstract, with no faces or figurative alterations. The second reference is Emmy's photographic portrait. The third reference is an example of art installed on the museum wall. Editorial cream exhibition catalogue, asymmetrical ruled grid. Large logo in deep maroon left of a stacked black Baskerville title 'The Human Touch' in top left. Tall portrait of Emmy on a velvet maroon field at right. Below, include the practical five-color palette (limestone cream, travertine, ink, velvet burgundy, aged brass), a 'Baskerville' and 'Avenir Next' typography specimen, small tactile photography of carved limestone, velvet and brass, a square brass with the EXACT logo engraved, and a beautifully framed museum exhibit. Extremely restrained type. Labels limited to 'Palette', 'Typography', 'Materials', and those two font names. Drawing room daylight, crisp legibility, museum-quality physical materials, warm light, precise gutters. No robot face as logo, no stock gradients, no invented text or interfaces. The humanoid appears only as a photo and in the artwork, never inside the identity mark.
